why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2 and 4 only test what their lines say: clamp is exported and limits x to the range, it throws a RangeError when lo > hi, and npm test passes. Check 3 is stricter than its line. "README.md documents every function math.js exports" says nothing about format. But the script's regex '^#+\s*name\s*\(' requires a Markdown heading for each function. The PASS condition says "each exported function has a heading", and FAIL says "any exported function has no heading in README.md". A README that documented subtract or clamp in a list, a table or prose would fail even though the line's words are met. This heading-format rule belongs under Advisory, not in the PASS/FAIL conditions, so the criterion does not hold.
